questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Whether the university had interesting courses and researchers (that would teach the courses) in the field I was interested in (media).
If the country was close to home, I have been traveling and living further away from home before, both geographically and culturally, and therefore, I was interested in going to a place that was similar to my home country.
It was also important for me to go to a country that I could see myself have a future in both work-wise but also personally, if I would be interested in living and working in another country in the future.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think the UvA were really good at giving us the right information, and taking care of us exchange students when we arrived at the university. It was clear that they are used to students coming from abroad, which made it a very nice experience.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university had general meetings for all exchange students, and there was also meetings in the faculty of humanities, which I was a part of, both with a lot of information that was valuable for incoming students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not easy at all. I found a room through a friend of a friend of a friend. Good connections is key to finding a place outside of the university's hosting opportunity, but generally it was very difficult, and I was really lucky to find the place I found.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it can also be lonely not to live on a campus and having a direct connection to fellow exchange students. You need to seek a social life more by yourself, so housing through the university might be better in that regard, but it's very individual what works for you. I also liked living in a "real" apartment, it made it easier to feel at home in the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't think there was enough information about the registration process, I ended up doing it wrong, and only registered for courses of 30 ects, when you were supposed to register for all the courses you were interested in, and thereafter choose which of them you wanted to take. I ended up having to register for random courses, since I didn't get the amount of courses that I needed in the first round, and by then most of the courses was filled up.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: UvA were very nice in helping me find available courses, so it was only information about the registration process that I needed more of.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very as explained. I got 3 out of 5 courses I was interested in.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To register for all the courses you are interested in, and then see which of them you get, and then choose which of them you'll take.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level was very suiting for the courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was much less personal, there were different teachers each module in some of the courses, which I liked, since they were experts in that certain topic.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Global Digital Culture
Privacy in Public
Encountering the Americas: Latin America in the 21st century
All-time bestsellers from Amsterdam
The meaning of having children

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Definitely:
Global Digital Culture
Privacy in Public

I think they were very interesting with super competent teachers.
But generally I had very good experiences in each course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There wasn't any unexpected costs, but it cost more to live there than I expected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything was generally more expensive. Grocery shopping, public transportation, and social life. So if you want to live in Amsterdam, you should prepare yourself that it will cost you a lot of money, that is not covered by Erasmus and SU (if you're from Denmark).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't use these opportunities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I'm not quite sure, because I didn't really look into what the university offered. But my impression from others is that there were a lot of opportunities for different activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely doing the Erasmus intro week, I found a lot of great friends in that week.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to other parts of the country as well – I enjoyed visiting Utrect. Otherwise, to use the city a lot, go for walks, check out what's new and happening. I followed a newsmagazine called AaMagazine, they posted a lot of great thing about what was happening in the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, Amsterdam was pretty similar to Copenhagen. But it's always difficult to adjust to a new city and country.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to locations that are typically dutch, if you live in Amsterdam. Like local bars and restaurants outside of centrum.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Dutch people can be quite direct, which can seem a bit rude. But otherwise it was very similar to home.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Dutch people say things as they are. And they are very good at 'using' the city, so being in the city, going out for dinner and drinks and so on. So everywhere you go, there is a lot of people, which gives a really nice and warm feeling to the city.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make sure to apply for enough courses.
Make sure to save up enough money, it costs a lot to live in Amsterdam.
Go to the Erasmus intro week, it gives you a really nice start to your stay. And arrive in the city in good time, so you can get settled before the intro-week begins, because it takes a lot of energy to socialize all the time.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't think so, I think I've mentioned it all.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know a new culture, meeting people from all over the world, and getting a break from your home-university, so I was filled with renewed motivation for my study field.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being alone in a new country, without your friends and family, and the loneliness that comes with that experience.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
